title: AI Product Video Generator for Demos | AIVideosUGC
description: Our AI product video generator shows your item in action, from a lid clicking shut to a lamp switching on. Make a short demo for Etsy, Shopify, or your ads.
h1: AI Product Video Generator for Showing How It Works
lead: Use an AI product video generator to plan a short demo around one visible action, such as a lid closing or a lamp switching on. Add a clear photo of that part and describe the movement you want to show.
intro: Product Videos focuses on one visible product action: a kettle pouring, a chair unfolding, or a drawer organizer holding cutlery. A focused demo can help shoppers understand how a feature works without turning one clip into a full tutorial.

With AIVideosUGC, upload a product photo and describe one action in a sentence. Pick the clip length and frame that suit the product action, from 6, 10, 15, or 30 seconds and 9:16, 1:1, 16:9, 4:3, or 3:4. It works well for home goods, kitchen tools, gadgets, bags, and other products where movement helps explain the feature.

benefits.d: A short clip of the lid opening or the light turning on explains more quickly than a list of specs.
Focused clips are easier to watch and easier to reuse. Make one for each feature and place them where they fit.
Choose 16:9 for a product page, 1:1 for listings, or 9:16 for YouTube Shorts, all from the same photo.

steps.t: Add a photo of the product
steps.d: Use a photo that shows the part that moves or opens, so the video has the right detail to work with.
Write what happens, such as “the lunch box lid clicks shut and the latch locks.” Then pick a size and 6, 10, 15, or 30 seconds.

steps.t: Save it or show another feature
steps.d: Download the clip, then write a new action to make a separate video for the next feature.

uses.d: According to Etsy Help's listing video guidance, videos can be 3–15 seconds and use a 2:1 or 1:2 aspect ratio. AIVideosUGC offers different ratios, so crop the downloaded clip in an editor and check it in Etsy before posting.
Place a wide or square demo with your product photos so shoppers see it work before they buy.
Post a vertical cut that shows one feature to reach people browsing Shorts.
If your seller account can add videos to listings, a short demo can sit next to your images.

faq.q: How is this different from image to video?
faq.a: Image to video adds requested camera movement to an existing still photo. A product demo focuses on one action, such as a zipper opening or a pump being pressed.

faq.q: Can I use the video on Etsy or Shopify?
faq.a: AIVideosUGC's frame choices differ from Etsy's listing-video ratios, so crop the download in an editor and check it in Etsy before posting. Shopify also lets you add video to product media.

faq.q: Will the video show my product accurately?
faq.a: Only describe actions your product can really do, and watch the clip before posting. If a button, color, or part looks different from the real item, make a new version rather than using that one.

faq.q: Can I add the price and product name?
faq.a: Add text later in Canva or CapCut. Letters generated by AI can come out garbled, so typed text is more reliable for names, prices, and dates.

overview.h2: Show one useful action, not a feature list
overview.p: A product demo earns its place when the motion answers a practical question: how a lid closes, how a switch works, how a bag opens, or how a part fits into the whole. Build one short clip around one action, then make another clip for the next feature.

overview.h2: Use the source photo to protect the details
overview.p: The starting image should make the moving component easy to see. If the action depends on a latch, hinge, handle, button, or opening, include that area in the photo and leave enough space for it to move.

input_guide.h2: Photograph the part that has to move

items.d: Aim the camera at the hinge, button, zipper, cap, latch, or handle that the action will use.

items.t: Keep the product fully in frame
items.d: Include enough of the surrounding object to show where the moving part belongs after it changes position.
A front, three-quarter, or side angle should make the intended direction understandable without a long explanation.
Write one action such as “the lid clicks shut and the latch locks” instead of asking for a complete how-to sequence.
Describe what the real product can do so the finished clip can be compared with the item a shopper will receive.
Generate 6, 10, 15, or 30 seconds around a single feature.
Use 9:16, 1:1, 16:9, 4:3, or 3:4 for the destination where the demo will appear.
Before generation, the editor shows what the job costs in credits; failed jobs return those credits.
The file has no watermark; the [FAQ](/faq) covers commercial-use terms. Review the mechanics and add approved text before posting.
A lunch box lid lowers onto the rim, then the front latch clicks into its locked position.
A folding chair opens beside a dining table while the seat settles flat and ready to use.
A hand turns the dial on a compact desk lamp and the pool of light grows across the work surface.
A drawer organizer slides into a kitchen drawer and holds spoons, forks, and chopsticks in separate sections.
A zipper travels across a travel pouch, revealing the divided pockets inside.
A glass carafe tips over a tumbler on a breakfast table while the handle remains visible.

after_download.h2: Approve the mechanics before you publish

items.t: Compare the action with the real item
items.d: Check the direction, proportions, moving parts, and final position against the product you sell.
Type product names, dimensions, prices, dates, or feature labels in your editor so the small details are correct.

items.t: Place clips beside the right photos
items.d: Use one focused demo near the feature it explains instead of asking one video to carry the whole listing.

fit.h2: When a product demo is the right format
good: Home goods with a clear open, close, fold, pour, or switch action
Kitchen tools where the handoff or latch matters
Bags, organizers, and accessories with useful compartments
Listings that need one moving explanation beside still photos
not_ideal: Products whose value depends mainly on an exact printed claim
Actions that require a real person to explain results aloud
